description:
The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of tokens and the Macro-F1 score for two different conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Number of tokens” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis is labeled “Macro-F1 Score (%)” and has a linear scale ranging from 48 to 59 with tick labels at intervals of 2. 

A pink line, representing “MATTER (ours)”, is plotted with circular markers and connects data points that begin at approximately 55% at x=0.5, rise to a peak of 58% at x=1.0, and then decline to approximately 50% at x=1.4. A shaded region surrounds the pink line, indicating variance. A purple line, representing “w/o material information”, is plotted with circular markers and connects data points that begin at 52.5% at x=0.5, rise to approximately 53% at x=0.7, and then stabilize around 52-53% for the remainder of the x-axis range, ending at approximately 48% at x=1.4. A shaded region surrounds the purple line, indicating variance, and there is overlap between the two shaded regions near x=1.2.
caption_used: Comparison of Macro-F1 scores for MATTER and w/o material knowledge during tokenization training across different numbers of tokens. The pink line representing MATTER (ours) starts at approximately 55% Macro-F1 Score, peaks at 58% near x=1.0, and ends at 50% near x=1.3, showing a consistent decline after its peak. The purple line, representing w/o material information, begins at 52.5%, peaks at 56% near x=0.7, and then stabilizes around 50% for the remainder of the range. The shaded areas indicate variance, with significant overlap between the two conditions near x=1.2. The results suggest that MATTER consistently outperforms the alternative across all token counts, with a sharper decline in performance at higher token counts for both conditions.
